name: Pol Pot
role: Leader of the Khmer Rouge and de facto ruler of Democratic Kampuchea (1975-1979)
summary: Pol Pot led the Communist Party of Kampuchea and ran Democratic Kampuchea, a one-party state that emptied the cities, abolished money, markets and religion, and collectivised agriculture under the Four-Year Plan. His own speeches stress independence and self-reliance, class struggle, and armed revolution; he saw Vietnam as the chief threat and purged party members as agents. Estimates of deaths under his rule run to 1.5-2 million.

notes: This pass revisited the October audit under rules 7. The ECCC judgment is cited for findings about what Pol Pot directed or carried out, and does not represent a criminal verdict against Pol Pot personally. I checked the record and his speeches by theme: economy and labor, government and elections, foreign policy and war, civil and political liberties, family and religion, culture and education, ecology and technology, revolutionary strategy, and relations with international institutions. The 1975–1979 record takes precedence where later interviews deny responsibility or describe different policies.
